live_target_cards.title: Open problem: Subdiffusive and KPZ passage-time fluctuation exponents
live_target_cards.body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Under suitable nondegenerate iid passage-time assumptions, prove a fluctuation exponent strictly below1/2, identify the planar exponent as1/3, and establish a positive exponent in a suitable dimension. Source: Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation, Questions13 and15, PDF pp.34 and40; Section3.
Posed in Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation

live_target_cards.title: Attempt on Subdiffusive and KPZ passage-time fluctuation exponents
live_target_cards.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Subdiffusive and KPZ passage-time fluctuation exponents structural argument Result: A variance upper bound of order n/log n does not establish an exponent below1/2. Indeed log(n/log n)/(2log n) tends to1/2. Sums of floor(n/log n) independent mean-zero variance-one variables realize that variance order in an elementary model. Check: The logarithm calculation is exact in the limit; the example has additive variances. It is not asserted to be FPP. Obstruction: Known sublinear-variance estimates leave a polynomial-exponent gap. An additional power saving, and a matching lower bound for identification, are required.
